The harsh reality is that relying on Stripe for digital commerce is a high-risk strategy for creators like you. Without infrastructure sovereignty, your online store can be shut down at a moment's notice, leaving you without a way to collect payments from your customers. Your customers own your digital products, but they have no access to the underlying infrastructure - a setup that can be disastrous in the face of platform restrictions. When Stripe is not an option, you need a permanent structural alternative that gives you full control over your digital commerce stack. That's where infrastructure sovereignty comes in.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Digital paypal

Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are all popular e-commerce platforms that offer a range of features and tools to help creators sell digital products. However, they all share one major limitation: they are not available in many parts of the world, particularly in Africa and Asia. This is because these platforms rely on a complex web of payment processors, banks, and regulatory frameworks that are not always accessible in these regions. In contrast, infrastructure sovereignty offers a base-layer approach that allows creators to deploy their own digital commerce stacks using free and open-source tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, and Supabase. This means that creators have full control over their infrastructure and can deploy it anywhere in the world, without relying on third-party platforms or payment processors.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe operates in only 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving millions of creators without access to this popular payment platform. PayPal, on the other hand, has a history of freezing accounts and holding funds for up to 180 days with no appeal, making it a high-risk option for creators in many countries. In contrast, infrastructure sovereignty is available to anyone with an internet connection and a willingness to learn. Creators can deploy their own digital commerce stacks using free and open-source tools, without relying on proprietary platforms or payment processors that may be restricted in their region.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Payment speed and fees are critical considerations for any e-commerce platform. Stripe, for example, charges a flat fee of 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction, while PayPal charges a flat fee of 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. In contrast, infrastructure sovereignty offers a flat fee of only 0.5% per transaction, making it a more cost-effective option for creators who want to keep their payment processing costs low. Additionally, infrastructure sovereignty offers faster payment processing times, with funds deposited directly into the creator's bank account within minutes of a sale.
Infrastructure sovereignty is the only way to guarantee that your digital commerce stack is not dependent on third-party platforms or payment processors.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

One of the key benefits of infrastructure sovereignty is that creators own and control their digital commerce stacks, giving them full autonomy over their business operations. This means that creators can automate their payment processing, delivery, and customer support workflows, freeing up time and resources to focus on creating more content and growing their business. Additionally, infrastructure sovereignty offers a range of tools and integrations that make it easy to manage and deliver digital products, including automatic delivery, tracking, and reporting.

So, which architecture should you choose based on your situation? If you're looking for a cost-effective solution that offers fast payment processing times and a low fee structure, then infrastructure sovereignty is the way to go. This stack includes Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Supabase, as well as NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. With the Edge Commerce Stack, you can deploy your digital commerce stack in just 48 hours and have it fully tested and configured before handoff. Additionally, you'll receive 30 days of support to help you get up and running quickly.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your own digital commerce stack using infrastructure sovereignty, follow these steps: 1) choose your hosting platform - GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages; 2) set up your payment processing - NOWPayments or another on-chain crypto payment processor; 3) configure your delivery and tracking workflows - using tools like Supabase or Google Sheets; 4) automate your customer support workflows - using tools like Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers; 5) deploy your digital commerce stack in just 48 hours - using the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) or another digital commerce builder. By following these steps, you can deploy your own digital commerce stack and say goodbye to platform restrictions once and for all.
